title: iF Design Award 2027
entryFee: From €400 per entry (regular, until Sep 18, 2026); €500 after
prizeMoney: iF Design Award trophy, seal, and global publicity (no cash prize)
shortDescription: One of the world's most prestigious design competitions, open to product, packaging, communication, interior, and UX design.
longDescription: The iF Design Award has run since 1954 and is judged by an independent panel of international experts across disciplines including product, packaging, communication, interior, and UX/UI design. Winning entries receive the iF seal, are published in the iF design app and yearbook, and are exhibited at iF's design centers in Hamburg and Taipei.
submissionFormat: Online entry with product images/renders; physical sample may be requested for the jury round

title: James Dyson Award 2026
entryFee: Free
prizeMoney: £30,000 international winner; £5,000 per national winner
shortDescription: An international student and recent-graduate award for engineering and product design that solves a real problem.
longDescription: Open to current and recent university students in engineering and design, the James Dyson Award rewards inventions that solve genuine, everyday problems. National winners are shortlisted before an international panel including James Dyson selects the global winner. The award emphasizes prototyping and iteration over polish.
submissionFormat: 1–2 A3 boards, a short process video, and supporting sketches submitted online

title: German Design Award 2027
entryFee: Free to register; participation fee applies once nominated
prizeMoney: German Design Award trophy and international recognition (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A cross-disciplinary award from the German Design Council, judged this cycle with a focus on communication design.
longDescription: Presented by the German Design Council, the German Design Award recognizes outstanding design work across product, communication, and architecture disciplines. Entrants must first be nominated before submitting; nominated work is judged by an independent jury of design experts, with winners announced at the awards show in Frankfurt.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the nomination platform: visuals plus a written project description

title: MUSE Design Awards 2026 (Season 2)
entryFee: $219–$269 professional entry depending on entry period (Regular through Last Minute) + $30 flat administrative fee
prizeMoney: MUSE trophy and global publicity (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A New York-based multidisciplinary design award spanning architecture, product, packaging, and graphic design.
longDescription: The MUSE Design Awards evaluate entries across dozens of subcategories, from architectural design to packaging and conceptual work. Judging is handled by a panel of design, media, and marketing professionals, and results include tiered Platinum, Gold, and Silver recognition rather than a single winner per category.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: images, a written description, and category-specific supporting material

title: A' Design Award & Competition 2026–2027
entryFee: Free to register; nomination fee applies only if shortlisted
prizeMoney: Trophy, gala presentation, and international press coverage
shortDescription: One of the largest global design competitions, covering over 100 categories including digital products and UX/UI.
longDescription: A' Design Award and Competition accepts entries across an unusually broad set of categories, including interface, interaction, and digital product design. Registration and initial submission are free; a nomination fee is only charged for entries that advance past preliminary review. Winners are announced annually on World Design Day, April 15.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: images, technical drawings, and a written design statement

title: Architecture MasterPrize 2026
entryFee: Tiered entry fee by deadline (early / regular / final pricing)
prizeMoney: Trophy and global publication (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international prize covering architectural design, interiors, landscape architecture, and architectural products.
longDescription: The Architecture MasterPrize invites built and unbuilt work from architects, interior designers, and landscape architects worldwide. Past editions have drawn entries from more than 70 countries. Winners are announced roughly a month after the final submission deadline and are featured in the organizer's annual publication.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: drawings, renders, photographs, and a project narrative

title: Interior Design Best of Year Awards 2026
organizer: SANDOW Design Group / Interior Design magazine
entryFee: From $285 (early bird) to $350 (late)
prizeMoney: Trophy and industry-wide recognition (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A long-running US interiors award covering completed projects and furniture/product design across many typologies.
longDescription: Interior Design's Best of Year Awards honor standout interiors and the products that furnish them, judged by a panel of practicing designers and editors. Categories span workplace, hospitality, residential, and healthcare interiors alongside furniture, lighting, and materials, with winners celebrated at an in-person ceremony.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: project or product photography, plans, and a written narrative

title: Bundespreis Ecodesign 2026
organizer: German Federal Ministry for the Environment / Umweltbundesamt
entryFee: Fee scales by company size; free for the student/newcomer (Nachwuchs) category
prizeMoney: Recognition award plus PR and communications support (no cash prize)
shortDescription: Germany's federal design award for products, services, and concepts with strong ecological performance.
longDescription: Presented by the German Federal Ministry for the Environment and the Umweltbundesamt, the Bundespreis Ecodesign recognizes companies, studios, and researchers whose work combines ecological responsibility with high design quality. A dedicated Nachwuchs (newcomer) category is open to students and graduates who finished their degree within the last year. This cycle's application window has closed; the entry remains listed for reference ahead of the next call.
submissionFormat: Online application with product/service documentation and ecological impact data

title: Green Product Award 2027
organizer: Green Product Award / Green Future Club
entryFee: Tiered entry fee (early bird / regular / final pricing)
prizeMoney: Trophy, certification seal, and audience award (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international award for sustainable products and services across 14 categories, from architecture to mobility.
longDescription: The Green Product Award has recognized sustainable products and services since 2012, inviting companies and start-ups to submit work across categories spanning architecture, consumer goods, mobility, and new materials. Nominees are published for public audience voting ahead of the final jury decision, with the award ceremony held in Berlin.
submissionFormat: Online submission: product images, a sustainability data sheet, and a written description

title: International Design Awards (IDA) 2026
entryFee: ~$250 per entry (professionals); ~$80 per entry (students), with early discounts
prizeMoney: Gold, Silver, and Bronze recognition plus press coverage (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A long-running Los Angeles-based award spanning architecture, interior, product, fashion, and graphic design.
longDescription: The International Design Awards recognize both professionals and students across five core disciplines: architecture, interior, product, fashion, and graphic design. Entries must have been completed within the last five years. Winners are graded Gold, Silver, or Bronze within each category, with top honorees also considered for Designer of the Year and Emerging Designer of the Year.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: images, technical details, and a project statement

title: Green Good Design Award 2027
organizer: The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design
entryFee: €375 per entry (+€25 if paying by bank transfer); +€100 late fee
prizeMoney: Trophy, exhibition, and international recognition (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international award for products, graphics, and organizations with strong ecological and sustainability credentials, presented by The Chicago Athenaeum.
longDescription: Part of the Good Design Award family administered by The Chicago Athenaeum and The European Centre for Architecture Art Design and Urban Studies, the Green Good Design Award recognizes work across six category groups: architecture, graphic design, organizations & people, product design, research & technology, and transportation. Winners are exhibited and published as part of the Good Design Awards program.
submissionFormat: Online submission: 4-6 project images (JPG/PNG, 300dpi) plus a written project description (max 500 words)

title: Communication Arts Typography Competition 2027
entryFee: From $40 per entry (varies by category); +$10 late fee after Sept 4, 2026; student discount available
prizeMoney: Publication in the Communication Arts Typography Annual (no cash prize)
shortDescription: One of the most prestigious competitions for typographic excellence, covering hand-lettering, calligraphy, and type design.
longDescription: Selected by a jury of distinguished designers and art directors, winning entries in the Communication Arts Typography Competition are published in the Typography Annual, included in the magazine's January/February issue and distributed worldwide. Entrants are notified within roughly two months of the deadline; entry fees vary by category with a discount for student submissions.
submissionFormat: Digital upload of high-resolution images or PDF documents showing the typographic work in context

title: European Product Design Award 2026
entryFee: €400 per entry (professional); students receive 50% off; 50% off each additional category when submitting the same design
prizeMoney: European Product Design Award Trophy for the European Product Designer of the Year and Discovery of the Year (student) titles; other winners receive certificates (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international product design award from Farmani Group recognizing innovation across categories like automotive, consumer electronics, and eco design.
longDescription: The European Product Design Award (EPDA) is organized by Farmani Group, the same organization behind the International Design Awards and Architecture MasterPrize. The competition draws entries from more than 58 countries across categories spanning automotive, consumer electronics, food and beverage, and eco design, judged by a jury of more than 30 international design leaders. The 2026 awards ceremony takes place in Venice.
submissionFormat: Online submission: 6–10 project images (professional photography preferred) plus a written project description; a supporting PDF may also be uploaded. A physical product sample is not required.

title: Tokyo TDC 2027 Annual Awards
entryFee: From $35 per entry in early submission (categories 1-8) up to $110 in final submission for larger categories; student rates run $20–$70 depending on category and timing
prizeMoney: Grand Prize: ¥200,000; other Prize-winning works: ¥100,000 each
shortDescription: A prestigious international typography and graphic design competition from the Tokyo Type Directors Club, open to designers worldwide.
longDescription: Tokyo TDC is one of the most respected typography and graphic design competitions internationally, evaluating work across multiple categories including typography, logotypes, packaging, and moving type. Entrants need not be professional type directors (applicants just need to have served as the type director on the submitted work), and a discounted student rate is available. Prize winners are notified in early December 2026, with results published online in mid-December 2026; the formal award ceremony (where prize money and diplomas are presented) and the accompanying exhibition run May 27 – July 8, 2027 at Ginza Graphic Gallery in Tokyo.
submissionFormat: Digital submission via the Tokyo TDC entry platform; category-specific image counts or PDF page counts depending on entry type

title: UX Design Awards 2027
entryFee: New Talent: €70 per submission; Product & Concept: €320 per submission (plus VAT); Nomination Package (Product & Concept): €2,250
prizeMoney: Nomination title, certificate, and trophy plus a PR/press campaign (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A biannual German award recognizing user-driven digital and physical products, concepts, and student projects in UX design.
longDescription: The UX Design Awards, organized by IDZ Designpartner Berlin, evaluate submissions across three tracks: Product (market-ready or soon-to-launch offerings), Concept (startups, prototypes, and research projects), and New Talent (bachelor's and master's degree projects). Judging emphasizes user-driven design and meaningful problem-solving, with nominees notified in December 2026 and winners announced in March 2027.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: 4 product images (JPEG, 3000×2000–4000×3000px), a project description (max. 500 characters), company/logo materials, plus optional promotional video and an R&D documentation PDF (max. ~10 pages) for jury review.

title: Buildner's Unbuilt Award 2026
entryFee: €140 (professional/company) or €120 (student) single registration fee, plus 4.5% VAT; registration open Jul 10 – Sep 23, 2026
prizeMoney: €100,000 total: 3 category winners (Small/Medium/Large) €20,000 each, 15 honorable mentions €1,000 each, 3 student prizes €5,000 each, best presentation award €10,000
shortDescription: An open international architecture prize for unbuilt (conceptual) projects, judged across small, medium, and large project scales with a dedicated student prize track.
longDescription: Organized by Buildner (formerly Bee Breeders), an established architecture-competition platform, the Unbuilt Award recognizes conceptual and unrealized architecture, interior, landscape, and furniture projects. Now in its third edition, entrants compete in Small, Medium, and Large categories, each with a €20,000 top prize, alongside honorable mentions, dedicated student prizes, and a best-presentation award, for a combined €100,000 prize fund. The competition is open to anyone regardless of professional qualification, entering individually or in teams of up to four.
submissionFormat: One anonymous A2 landscape panel (max 10MB) with visuals and explanatory text in English; video and animation are not permitted

title: Communication Arts 2027 Illustration Competition
entryFee: Varies by category (published in the organizer's Category Fee schedule); student entries receive substantial discounts
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive a personalized aluminum Award of Excellence, worldwide publication in the Illustration Annual, and printed certificates
shortDescription: A long-running global illustration competition from Communication Arts magazine; winners are published in the print and digital Illustration Annual.
longDescription: Open to illustrators worldwide, the Communication Arts Illustration Competition accepts any illustration first published or produced between January 2026 and January 2027 (AI text-to-image submissions are excluded). Winners receive a personalized aluminum Award of Excellence, worldwide publication in the Illustration Annual, and a feature on the Communication Arts website. Entry fees vary by category, with substantial discounts for student entrants.
submissionFormat: Digital images as RGB JPG (max 2MB) or motion/animation as MOV, MP4, MPG, or GIF (max 500MB), submitted through the online competition system

title: Green Concept Award 2027
organizer: Green Product Award / Green Future Club
entryFee: €450 (free for students and graduates within 6 months of graduation)
prizeMoney: No cash prize: finalists receive digital certificates, personalized jury feedback, an online project gallery profile, and rights to use finalist/winner seals
shortDescription: Sibling award to the Green Product Award for early-stage sustainable design concepts and prototypes, with free entry for students.
longDescription: The Green Concept Award, run by the Green Future Club alongside the established Green Product Award, recognizes sustainability-focused design concepts and prototypes across 14 categories. Applicants must provide verifiable sustainability evidence supported by documentation. Finalists receive digital certificates, personalized jury feedback, and an online profile in the project gallery; the awards ceremony takes place in Berlin.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the gp-award.com portal with supporting sustainability documentation

title: WIN Awards 2026
entryFee: £585 + VAT per entry
prizeMoney: No cash prize identified in available materials. Winners are recognized at the WIN Awards ceremony and in press/industry coverage; specific trophy or certificate details were not published on the official site
shortDescription: Annual international awards recognizing outstanding interior design projects across residential, commercial, and public spaces, organized by World Interiors News.
longDescription: Now in its 14th year, the WIN Awards (World Interiors News Awards) celebrate innovative, visionary interior design work worldwide across 27 categories spanning residential, commercial, and public spaces. Entries are judged by an international jury of design professionals. The 2026 edition is open for submissions with a final deadline of August 6, 2026; winners are announced in November 2026 (exact date not yet published).
submissionFormat: Online submission via the WIN Awards portal (win-awards.evessiocloud.com): project details, design features, materials, and supporting images per category. Exact image/word-count specifications are provided in the site's downloadable Entry Kit.

title: London Design Awards 2026 (Season 2)
entryFee: $30 flat administrative fee plus $209–$249 per category entry, depending on submission period
prizeMoney: No cash prize: Design of the Year winners receive a complimentary limited-edition LITO trophy and certificate; Platinum/Gold/Silver winners may purchase additional trophies or customized certificates. All winners get marketing benefits (social media post, winner interview, profile page, press release template, winner badge); Platinum/Gold winners are also featured in the LDA online gallery and on IAA/Muse.World social channels.
shortDescription: International, multi-discipline design competition covering 12 categories including product, architecture, UX/UI, and communication design, run by International Awards Associate.
longDescription: The London Design Awards is organized by International Awards Associate (IAA), the same organization behind the MUSE Design Awards. Season 2 of the 2026 program spans 12 categories, including Product Design, Architectural Design, Interior Design, User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) Design, and Communication Design, and is open to designers, studios, and brands of all backgrounds. Season 2 entries are accepted in tiers through a Final Extension deadline of November 6, 2026, with results announced December 18, 2026.
submissionFormat: Fully online submission: a project synopsis of roughly 350 words, flattened JPEG/JPG images (under 4MB, ~1,200px wide, 300dpi, RGB), an optional supporting PDF brief, and video/audio submitted via a Vimeo/YouTube/Youku URL. Physical product samples are not required.

title: KOKUYO Design Award 2027
entryFee: Free
prizeMoney: Grand Prix (1 winner): ¥2,000,000 (~$13,000); Merit Award (3 winners): ¥500,000 (~$3,200) each; New Generation Award (up to 10 student winners): ¥30,000 (~$200) each. Amounts stated are after applicable Japanese tax withholding.
shortDescription: International product design competition from Japanese stationery and furniture maker KOKUYO, open worldwide with a dedicated student category, themed 'dialogue' for 2027.
longDescription: KOKUYO DESIGN AWARD is an international product design competition run by KOKUYO Co., Ltd., a major Japanese stationery, office furniture, and workspace-tools manufacturer. Entries are open worldwide to individuals, groups, and corporations for original, previously unpublished designs of stationery, furniture, or tools used in working, learning, and living. The 2027 edition is themed 'dialogue,' accepts entries free of charge, and includes a New Generation Award judged separately from all student submissions (elementary school through graduate level). Submissions opened July 24, 2026 and close at noon JST on October 7, 2026, with results announced March 13, 2027.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the KOKUYO Design Award entry portal: entrant registration plus design proposal materials (visuals and a written description) uploaded through the site's ENTRY pages. Detailed file-format specifications are provided within the entry portal itself.

title: AIA International Design Awards 2026
entryFee: $350 USD (AIA International members) / $475 USD (AIA US-chapter members); non-members must also purchase current-year AIA membership to enter
prizeMoney: No cash prize identified: winners receive AIA International Honor Award or Merit Award designation, recognition at the AIA International Conference (Cairo, November 2026) and the AIA Conference on Architecture and Design (Philadelphia, 2027), plus features on the AIA International website and in publications.
shortDescription: American Institute of Architects awards program honoring architecture, interior architecture, urban design, and unbuilt projects located outside the United States.
longDescription: The AIA International Design Awards, run by the American Institute of Architects' International chapter, recognize built and unbuilt work by AIA-affiliated architects on projects located anywhere outside the US and its territories. The 2026 program spans seven categories: Architecture, Interior Architecture, Urban Design, Unbuilt Projects, Firm Award, Sustainable Future Award (developed with Dow), and Inclusive Design Excellence Award. Non-AIA members may enter but must complete an AIA membership application as part of submission. The 2026 submission deadline is Friday, August 14, 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern US time, with winners celebrated at the AIA International Conference in Cairo on November 14, 2026.
submissionFormat: Primary jury-review submission is a PDF (max 20 pages, max 10MB) with at least 3 project photographs plus floor plans, site plans, elevations, and sections. Separate high-resolution (300dpi+) images are required for exhibition/publication if the entry is selected.

title: Red Dot Award: Product Design 2027
organizer: Red Dot GmbH & Co. KG (Design Zentrum Nordrhein Westfalen)
entryFee: Tiered entry fee by registration phase (early bird / standard / late submission); exact 2027 amounts not yet published
prizeMoney: Red Dot trophy, quality label license, and international publicity (no cash prize for the main Product Design award)
shortDescription: One of the world's most prestigious product design competitions, recognizing outstanding product design across industries worldwide.
submissionFormat: Online registration and entry via the My Red Dot portal, with a separate registration required for each entry
longDescription: The Red Dot Award: Product Design is one of the largest and most renowned design competitions in the world, run by Design Zentrum Nordrhein Westfalen. Registration for the 2027 edition opens 14 September 2026 and runs through the late submission deadline of 15 January 2027, in early bird, standard, and late-submission phases with increasing fees. The award is open to manufacturers and designers worldwide whose products are made using an industrial production process and launched on the market between 1 January 2025 and 1 July 2027. Entrants register and submit via the My Red Dot online portal, with a separate registration required for each entry. Winners are notified by email at the beginning of April 2027, and the Red Dot: Best of the Best trophies are awarded at a gala evening at the Aalto Theatre in Essen, Germany, on 13 July 2027.

title: American Architecture Awards 2027
organizer: The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design
entryFee: $395 USD per entry online (plus $50 fee for bank transfer; $100 late fee applies after the deadline)
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners are exhibited internationally and published in the Metropolitan Arts Press catalog
shortDescription: Annual program from The Chicago Athenaeum honoring outstanding American architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning projects.
submissionFormat: Online application via awardapplication.com: a 500-1000 word project description, 10-12 images (16:9 or 1:1, 300dpi, max 6MB each), and a single PDF (max 25MB) of floor plans, sections, and elevations
longDescription: The American Architecture Awards, presented by The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design, recognize commercial, corporate, institutional, healthcare, transportation, educational, and residential buildings as well as urban planning projects, across more than 32 categories including specialized areas like energy buildings and restoration work. Eligible submissions must be the work of American architects, landscape architects, or urban planners (including international firms with U.S. offices) for projects built or unbuilt in the U.S., or by U.S. firms working abroad, since 1 January 2025. The submission deadline for the 2027 edition is 1 February 2027. Winning projects are exhibited internationally and published in the Metropolitan Arts Press catalog.

title: Communication Arts 2027 Photography Competition
entryFee: Varies by category (published in the organizer's Category Fee schedule); $10 per-entry late fee for entries between March 12–26, 2027
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive a personalized aluminum Award of Excellence, publication in the Communication Arts Photography Annual (print and digital), and a certificate
shortDescription: International photography competition from Communication Arts magazine, honoring outstanding work across advertising, editorial, and other categories.
submissionFormat: Online submission: digital images as JPG/RGB (max 2MB) or motion entries as MOV/MP4/MPG (max 500MB)
longDescription: The Communication Arts Photography Competition is an annual international competition recognizing excellence in advertising, book, editorial, institutional, self-promotion, motion/cinematography, and unpublished photography, plus a dedicated Student Work category. Any photograph first published or produced between March 2026 and March 2027 is eligible, with entries accepted from any country; AI-generated submissions are excluded. The deadline for the 2027 competition is 12 March 2027 (midnight Pacific Time), with late entries accepted until 26 March 2027 for a $10 per-entry surcharge. There is no cash prize; winners receive a personalized solid aluminum Award of Excellence, a certificate, and publication in the Communication Arts Photography Annual (print and digital) along with online exposure. Only accepted entrants are notified, within about two months of the final deadline.

title: DNA Paris Design Awards 2027
entryFee: €350 per entry (Architecture, Interior, Product); €100 per entry (Graphic); €75 per entry for students in any category, with 50% off each additional category; 20% early-bird discount until Dec 18, 2026, 10% extended early-bird until Feb 19, 2027; +10% late fee for entries between the May 7 regular deadline and the May 21, 2027 final deadline
prizeMoney: DNA Award trophy; main category winners are named 'DNA Designer of the Year' (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A Paris-based multidisciplinary design award spanning architecture, interior, landscape, product, and graphic design, open to both professionals and students.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the DNA Paris entry portal: project images and a written description, with category-specific supporting material
longDescription: The DNA Paris Design Awards recognize outstanding work across five main disciplines: architecture, interior design, landscape, product design, and graphic design. Separate, lower-cost entry tiers are available for student submissions. Entrants can apply for up to five sub-awards within their main category. Main category winners are named DNA Designer of the Year, and all winners are celebrated at an annual awards ceremony in Paris.

title: A' Sustainable Products, Projects and Green Design Award 2026
entryFee: Registration is free; a nomination fee applies once shortlisted and scales by entry edition (Digital / Vision / Classic / Pro); exact 2026 amounts not published on the fee calculator page found this session
prizeMoney: A' Design Prize package of PR, marketing, and publicity tools for professional-edition laureates, plus trophy and gala presentation (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A sustainability-focused track of the long-running A' Design Award, recognizing sustainable products, projects, and green design across a broad range of industries.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the A' Design Award competition platform: images, technical details, and a written design statement
longDescription: Run by the same organization behind the flagship A' Design Award & Competition, the A' Sustainable Products, Projects and Green Design Award evaluates entries spanning eco-friendly furniture, sustainable architecture and interiors, renewable energy projects, green industrial design, and dozens of related categories. Professional-edition laureates receive the A' Design Prize, a package of PR, marketing, and publicity tools, and are celebrated at the annual gala presentation.

title: SDGs Design International Awards 2026
organizer: SDGs Design International Awards Committee (Kyushu University, Japan & Dongseo University, Korea)
entryFee: Free (no entry fee stated across the official pages found this session)
prizeMoney: Gold Award: KRW 3,000,000 + certificate; Silver Award: KRW 2,000,000 + certificate; Bronze Award: KRW 1,000,000 + certificate; Honorable Mention and Special High School Award: e-certificate
shortDescription: A binational academic design competition from Kyushu University (Japan) and Dongseo University (Korea) for student ideas addressing the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
submissionFormat: Word or PDF application form submitted by email to the organizing committee, per the format specified in the official call for entries
longDescription: The SDGs Design International Awards invite university, graduate school, vocational, and high school students worldwide (including those outside design programs) to propose creative design solutions to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Entries fall under four themes: Resilient Cities and Communities, Sustainable Green Design and Climate Action, Blue Sustainability (Oceans and Water), and other related topics. The competition is jointly organized by the design faculties of Kyushu University and Dongseo University.

title: Pavilion Atlas 2026
entryFee: €140 (architects/professionals/companies) or €120 (students) single registration fee, payable in full or via 3 monthly installments; registration open through Sep 16, 2026
prizeMoney: €20,000 total: 1st €10,000, 2nd €5,000, 3rd €3,000, Student Award €1,000, Sustainability Award €1,000, plus 6 honorable mentions
shortDescription: An international conceptual pavilion design competition from Buildner and ArchDaily, open to architects, artists, and creatives of all backgrounds.
submissionFormat: Digital submission of a conceptual pavilion design and supporting narrative, submitted in English via the Buildner platform
longDescription: Pavilion Atlas, organized by Buildner in partnership with ArchDaily, invites entrants to design a conceptual pavilion for a country of their choice, conveying a spatial narrative about that place. Open to architects, artists, and creatives regardless of professional qualification, entries are judged with dedicated prizes for students and for sustainability-focused designs, alongside the main placings. All submissions must be in English.

title: Kingspan MICROHOME 2026
entryFee: €140 (professional/enthusiast) or €120 (student) single registration fee plus 4.5% VAT, payable in full or via installments; registration open through Sep 30, 2026
prizeMoney: €100,000 total prize fund: €55,000 in Buildner prizes (1st €30,000, 2nd €10,000, 3rd €5,000, plus Student and Sustainability Awards), plus a separate €30,000 Kingspan Award and three €5,000 Kingspan Compliments
shortDescription: A Buildner and Kingspan-sponsored international competition to design a sustainable, energy-efficient microhome under 25m², open to all backgrounds.
submissionFormat: Four A2 presentation panels (suggested, not mandatory) submitted in English via the Buildner platform
longDescription: Now in its 11th edition, Kingspan MICROHOME challenges architects, designers, and creative thinkers to develop a modular, self-sufficient, energy-efficient microhome with a maximum footprint of 25 square meters for a hypothetical young professional couple. The competition is open to entrants of any professional background and includes dedicated Buildner Student and Sustainability Awards alongside the main placings and the sponsor-funded Kingspan Award. All submissions must be in English.

title: The Architect's Chair – Stockholm Furniture Fair Edition #6
organizer: Buildner (in partnership with Stockholm Furniture Fair)
entryFee: Advanced tier (24 Jul – 24 Sep 2026): €120 professional / €110 student; Last Minute tier (25 Sep – 3 Dec 2026): €140 professional / €120 student, plus 4.5% VAT; registration closes 3 December 2026
prizeMoney: €8,000 total prize fund: 1st €3,500, 2nd €2,000, 3rd €1,000, Student Award €1,000, Sustainability Award €500, plus 6 honorable mentions
shortDescription: A Buildner and Stockholm Furniture Fair competition inviting architects and designers to distill their design philosophy into a single signature chair or seating piece.
submissionFormat: Digital submission via the Buildner platform: renders/visuals of the furniture design and a supporting narrative, in English; physical prototypes not required
longDescription: Now in its sixth edition, The Architect's Chair challenges entrants to design a piece of furniture (following in the tradition of Eames, Mies van der Rohe, and Jacobsen) that expresses their architectural thinking in object form. Open to architects, artists, students, and creatives of any professional background working individually or in teams of up to four, entries may include benches and stools alongside chairs; renders are accepted and physical prototypes are not required. Winners are exhibited at the Stockholm Furniture Fair and published on ArchDaily.

title: DIELINE Awards 2027
entryFee: Tiered by entry window and eligibility tier: Professional $295–$545, Independent $195–$425, Concept/Student/Design-for-Good $95–$215, rising across nine deadline windows from Early Bird (July 1, 2026) through Late Entry (February 27, 2027)
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive a custom digital seal, feature coverage on DIELINE, and exhibition in the annual Winner Showcase; one Best of Show winner (chosen from the five highest-scoring entries) also receives a Crystal Clear trophy and a global press release
shortDescription: A leading global packaging design and CPG design competition from DIELINE, spanning consumer packaging categories from food and beverage to circular/refill design.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the DIELINE Awards platform: packaging photography/renders and a written project description, per category
longDescription: The DIELINE Awards, run by packaging-design publication DIELINE, recognize excellence across consumer packaging and CPG design. The 2027 edition expands to include five new categories: Brand Worlds & Experiential, Functional Innovation & Accessibility, Retail/POS & Merchandising, Connected Packaging & Digital, and Circular, Refill & Reuse, alongside deeper subcategory coverage in Health & Beauty, Food, Beverage, and Home. Entries span Professional, Independent, and a restructured Concept/Student track, with every submission reviewed by DIELINE's editorial team for potential feature coverage regardless of judging outcome.

title: IIDA Global Excellence Awards 2026
entryFee: Early-Bird (Sep 1–8, 2026): $350 members / $450 non-members; Regular (Sep 9–Oct 5): $450 / $550; Last Chance (Oct 6–13): $550 / $650
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners are celebrated at an awards ceremony in Paris, featured on IIDA.org and social media, and receive digital winner assets plus press-release coverage to industry outlets
shortDescription: IIDA's flagship international interior design awards program, honoring interior design and interior architecture projects located outside the United States.
submissionFormat: Online submission via IIDA's official competition portal, including project imagery and a written project narrative
longDescription: Now in its 17th year, the IIDA Global Excellence Awards recognize originality and creativity in interior design and interior architecture across 19 categories, including corporate, hospitality, healthcare, education, retail, and residential spaces. Any interior designer, interior architect, or architect worldwide may submit, provided the project itself is located outside the United States and was completed within the previous two years. Winners are celebrated at an in-person ceremony in Paris.

title: World Design Awards 2026
entryFee: Super Early discount (Nov 30, 2025 – Mar 1, 2026): $150; Regular fee (Mar 2 – Oct 31, 2026): $250
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive a trophy, certificate, a published book feature, and promotional exposure across The Architecture Community's platforms and media partners
shortDescription: An international architecture and design award covering commercial, residential, interior, landscape, and urban design projects, open to architects, students, and designers worldwide.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: up to 4 A3-size JPG sheets (RGB), a cover image, a written project description (DOC file), and a studio brief, submitted as a single zip file (max 80MB) via the online portal
longDescription: Run by The Architecture Community (the organization behind World Architecture Community / worldarchitecture.org, active since the mid-2000s), the World Design Awards recognize built and concept work across more than 20 categories spanning commercial, residential, institutional, and interior architecture as well as landscape, urban design, and temporary structures. Entries are judged by separate design and architecture panels and are open globally to architects, engineers, designers, students, and artists, with no restriction on project completion date or concept stage.

title: 2026 Brick in Architecture Awards
entryFee: Per-entry fee required via the my.gobrick.com submission portal; exact 2026 dollar amount not published in sources found this session
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive Best in Class, Gold, Silver, or Bronze recognition within their category, plus an overall Craftsmanship Award, and are honored at the Brick Excellence Gala
shortDescription: A US architecture award from the Brick Industry Association honoring outstanding built projects that showcase clay brick, judged across nine categories.
submissionFormat: Entries are submitted through the my.gobrick.com portal per the official Rules & Regulations; exact image/document specifications were not confirmed in sources found this session
longDescription: Presented annually by the Brick Industry Association (BIA), the Brick in Architecture Awards recognize residential, commercial, educational, and historic-renovation projects in which new clay brick forms more than half of the visible exterior surface. Entrants must be architects or designers at architectural, design-build, or landscape architecture firms, and eligible projects must have been completed on or after January 1, 2020. Entries compete within nine categories for Best in Class, Gold, Silver, or Bronze recognition, plus an overall Craftsmanship Award; a peer jury judges submissions in October, with winners celebrated at the Brick Excellence Gala during the National Clay Brick Expo in Nashville.

title: Graphis Poster Awards 2027
entryFee: Tiered by submission window (early/regular/final); Graphis Members receive 50% off. Exact 2027 dollar amounts were not published in sources found this session. The sibling Graphis Design Awards 2027 used Early Bird (members $70/non-members $140), Regular ($120/$240), and Final ($140/$280) tiers, which may not carry over exactly to Poster Awards pricing
prizeMoney: No cash prize: Platinum and Gold winners receive certificates and publication in the Graphis Poster Annual, with recognition on graphis.com and in Graphis's newsletter
shortDescription: A long-running New York-based international poster design competition from Graphis, recognizing excellence in poster design by industry professionals.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the Graphis entry platform: a digital image of the poster design plus project details, per Graphis's standard entry requirements (exact file specs not confirmed in sources found this session)
longDescription: Graphis Poster Awards is an annual professional-only poster design competition run by Graphis, Inc., the New York publisher behind the Graphis Design, Advertising, and New Talent competitions. Work must be produced by industry professionals within the past two years; student work is directed instead to Graphis's separate New Talent competition. Winners are announced in a blog post, online gallery, and newsletter on graphis.com, and Platinum/Gold-winning work is published in the print Graphis Poster Annual.

title: 31st Annual Webby Awards
organizer: International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences (IADAS)
entryFee: Tiered pricing with an early-bird discount of $80 per entry before the August 22, 2026 early-bird deadline; exact 2027 dollar amounts were not published in sources found this session
prizeMoney: No cash prize: Webby and People's Voice winners receive the Webby Award trophy, global press coverage, and recognition at the Webby Awards ceremony in New York
shortDescription: The Webby Awards, presented by the International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences, honor excellence across websites, apps, and other digital experiences, with a dedicated Websites & Mobile Sites category judged partly on UX/UI design.
submissionFormat: Online submission via webbyawards.com: a live URL or app link plus a written project description, per category-specific entry guidelines
longDescription: Founded in 1998, the Webby Awards are presented by the International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences (IADAS), a 3,000+ member judging body of internet and digital-media professionals. Entries span eight media types including Websites & Mobile Sites and Apps, Software & Immersive, evaluated on criteria that include usability and user experience alongside content and creativity. The competition is open globally to individuals, brands, and organizations, with an early-bird pricing window and a final entry deadline each fall; winners are announced the following spring and celebrated at a ceremony in New York.

title: L.A.M.P International Lighting Design Competition 2026
entryFee: A submission fee applies (funds the competition, prize money, and marketing for finalists per the organizer); exact 2026 dollar amount not published in sources found this session. A Late deadline runs through October 15, 2026 at an increased fee
prizeMoney: Public recognition plus cash awards for standout designs; exact prize amounts not published in sources found this session
shortDescription: An independent international lighting design competition open to both professional and student designers, with finalists selected across Professional, Student, and Manufactured categories.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the L.A.M.P Submittable portal (xlampthecompetition.submittable.com); exact file/document requirements were not confirmed in sources found this session
longDescription: L.A.M.P is an independent, small-organization international lighting design competition focused on championing emerging talent and connecting lighting designers to new markets. The 2026 edition is open to Professional and Student entrants, with past editions also recognizing a Manufactured category for lighting products already in production. Submission and sponsorship fees fund the competition's prize money and marketing support for finalists. The competition has been covered by design press including Azure Magazine, Design Milk, and Bustler.

title: DBA Design Effectiveness Awards 2027
entryFee: DBA Members receive one complimentary entry then a discounted per-entry rate (£595+VAT in the 2025 cycle); Non-members pay a standard per-entry rate (£1,120+VAT in 2025), with an early-booking discount (~£100+VAT off). Exact 2027 figures were not published in sources found this session
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive Bronze, Silver, or Gold recognition, announced at The Design Effect industry event in London
shortDescription: The UK's longest-running awards program for measuring the commercial impact of design, jointly entered by the design team or agency and the client who commissioned the work.
submissionFormat: Two-part submission via the DBA's entry platform: an anonymous case study (max 9 pages) for judging, plus a publication version (max 12 pages) if shortlisted; entries must include measurable evidence dated after 1 June 2024, plus a signed sign-off from senior leadership at both the design team/agency and the client
longDescription: Run by the Design Business Association (DBA) and established in 1989, the Design Effectiveness Awards are the longest-running program dedicated to demonstrating the business impact of design, using commercial data as a core judging criterion alongside creative merit. Entries are open globally, but must be submitted jointly by the agency or in-house design team that delivered the work and the client who commissioned it, backed by measurable evidence of the work's effect on the business. Winners receive Gold, Silver, or Bronze recognition and are celebrated at The Design Effect industry event in London.

title: Architizer A+Awards 2027 (15th Annual)
entryFee: Tiered by deadline: $275 USD (Oct 23, 2026) rising to $425 USD (Feb 19, 2027), plus an optional $195 USD Project of the Year consideration fee and a 3% payment processing surcharge
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners are published in the annual hardbound book 'Architizer: The World's Best Architecture' and celebrated online and at in-person events
shortDescription: The industry's largest international architecture awards program, judged by a jury of hundreds of professionals plus an online public vote across dozens of building typologies.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the Architizer A+Awards platform: project images/renders, a written project description, and category-specific supporting material
longDescription: Organized by Architizer, the A+Awards is one of the largest international architecture awards programs, reviewing thousands of submissions each year across typology categories (residential, commercial, cultural, institutional, and more), Plus Categories addressing contemporary issues, and dedicated Sustainability and Student Project categories. Entries are judged by a jury of several hundred professionals from architecture, design, and related fields, combined with an online public vote. Winners are published in the annual hardbound compendium 'Architizer: The World's Best Architecture.'

title: Open Chair Design Competition 2026
entryFee: Early Bird: £5 (individual) / £10 (team); Regular: £15 / £25; Late: £25 / £35
prizeMoney: £1,000 total: 1st place £600, 2nd place £300, 3rd place £100, plus 5 honorable mentions (certificates)
shortDescription: A global ideas competition challenging designers to create a full-scale chair that can be 3D-printed at home and assembled with minimal tools.
submissionFormat: Digital submission (max 15MB combined): two 3D-print files (.STL) showing the assembled chair and individual parts, an A2 landscape board (JPG) with visualizations and an assembly guide, an A2 portrait poster (JPG), and a project description (PDF, max 500 words)
longDescription: Open Chair, run by UK-based Creathlon in partnership with Aibuild, invites students, professionals, and design enthusiasts worldwide to reimagine the chair through the lens of digital fabrication and open-source design. Entrants submit a full-scale chair designed to be 3D-printed on a home printer, assembled with minimal tools, and shared as a reproducible design for others to build. Teams are permitted alongside individual entries.

title: International Sustainable Building Competition 2026
organizer: UNEP, Global Alliance for Buildings and Construction (GlobalABC), and Türkiye Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change
entryFee: Free
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive a certificate of honour and international recognition at COP31
shortDescription: A UN- and Türkiye-backed international competition recognizing energy-efficient, low-carbon, climate-resilient buildings, with winners honored at COP31 in Antalya.
submissionFormat: Online application via yesint.csb.gov.tr with 3–4 project photographs uploaded directly through the site
longDescription: Organized by UNEP, the Global Alliance for Buildings and Construction (GlobalABC), and Türkiye's Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change, the International Sustainable Building Competition invites architects and building professionals worldwide to submit built projects and masterplans that demonstrate energy-efficient, low-carbon, and climate-resilient design. The competition is free to enter and is timed to coincide with COP31, the UN Climate Change Conference hosted in Antalya, Türkiye in November 2026, where winning projects will be honored.

title: NY Product Design Awards 2026 (Season 2)
entryFee: $219 USD for the first entry plus a $30 USD annual administrative fee; $219 USD per additional category for the same work (non-refundable)
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive the 'Ava' statuette plus marketing and publicity benefits
shortDescription: An International Awards Associate program recognizing product design across 17 categories including lighting, automotive, furniture, and wearable technology.
submissionFormat: Fully online submission: flattened JPEG/JPG images (under 4MB, ~1,200px wide, 300dpi, RGB), a project synopsis of roughly 350 words, and optional video/audio via a Vimeo/YouTube/Youku URL; physical product samples are optional
longDescription: The NY Product Design Awards is organized by International Awards Associate (IAA), the organization behind the MUSE Design Awards and London Design Awards. Season 2 of the 2026 program spans 17 categories, from lighting and automotive/transport to furniture, packaging, digital devices, medical equipment, and wearable technology, and is open to product designers, design teams, and manufacturers worldwide. Winners receive the 'Ava' statuette along with marketing and publicity benefits.

title: Spark Design Awards 2026 (Fall/Winter Cycle)
entryFee: Two-phase fee: Phase 1 registration (Late/Fall deadline) is US$675 for most professional categories (US$430 for Graphic Design, lower for students); entries shortlisted as Finalist Candidates pay an additional US$575 Phase 2 fee ahead of the live jury round
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive Platinum, Gold, Silver, or Bronze recognition (or the 'Greatest Design of the Year' title), a certificate, logo rights, and inclusion in the online Winners Gallery
shortDescription: A long-running, budget-friendly multidisciplinary design competition spanning product, architecture, interiors, graphic, and digital design, judged through a two-phase jury process.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the Spark Awards registration portal: project images and a written description, per category-specific requirements; shortlisted finalists undergo an additional live jury review
longDescription: Founded in 2001 by producer Peter Kuchnicki, the Spark Awards (International Design Competition) is a multidisciplinary program spanning Product & Industrial Design, Spaces Design (architecture, interiors, landscape, and urban planning), Graphic Design, Digital Design (UX/UI, apps, motion), Packaging, Transport & Mobility, Health/Medical/Universal Design, and a dedicated Student Design track. Judging uses a two-phase process: an initial registration and jury round determines shortlisted Finalist Candidates, who then pay a second fee ahead of a live jury session that selects Platinum, Gold, Silver, and Bronze winners. The current cycle's final deadline runs through November 19, 2026 for professionals and November 25, 2026 for students.

title: LIT Lighting Design Awards 2026
entryFee: Professional: CHF 230 (~US$250) per entry incl. Swiss VAT (50% off each additional category); Student: CHF 100 (~US$106) per entry (50% off each additional category); a 10% late fee applies during the final entry window (Sep 30 – Oct 18, 2026)
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive recognition titles (e.g. Lighting Design of the Year, Emerging Lighting Designer of the Year), inclusion in the annual catalogue, and are celebrated at an in-person awards ceremony
shortDescription: An international lighting design competition covering lighting products, architectural lighting, and entertainment lighting, marking its 10-year anniversary in 2026.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the LIT Awards entry portal: project images/renders and a written description, per category-specific requirements
longDescription: Organized by Farmani Group (the same organization behind the International Design Awards, Architecture MasterPrize, and European Product Design Award), the LIT Lighting Design Awards recognize excellence in Lighting Product Design, Entertainment Lighting Design, and Architectural Lighting Design, alongside special Lifetime Achievement and Spotlight prizes. Now marking its 10th anniversary, the 2025 edition drew entries from 62 countries. Winners are celebrated at an in-person gala (Paris hosted the 2024 and 2025 ceremonies) and featured in the annual LIT catalogue.

title: Indigo Design Award 2026
entryFee: Freelancer entries from US$150 (+US$50 per additional category); Early Bird (through Sep 30, 2026): 15% discount; Extended Early Bird (through Nov 30, 2026): 10% discount; full price applies after. Agency and student rates differ; exact current tier amounts were not confirmed in sources found this session
prizeMoney: No cash prize confirmed: winners receive portfolio visibility, recognition across 46+ countries, and features in Indigo's design-community promotion. Specific trophy/certificate details were not confirmed in sources found this session
shortDescription: An independent, Lisbon-based international design competition for graphic and digital design, judged by a jury of professionals from major tech and agency brands, with reduced entry fees for freelancers and students.
submissionFormat: Online submission: up to 10 images per entry (JPG/PNG, max 5MB each), with an optional supporting PDF
longDescription: Founded in 2017 and run by Marly Group Limited in Lisbon, Portugal, the Indigo Design Award evaluates work across four categories: Graphic Design, Digital Design (including UX/UI), Branding, and Design for Social Change. Entrants include agencies, freelancers, and students, judged by an international jury drawn from companies including Google, Microsoft, Nike, Spotify, and IBM. The competition emphasizes accessibility for smaller studios and independent designers, with tiered pricing and a published refund policy.

title: Design Intelligence Award (DIA) 2026
organizer: Design Intelligence Award Committee (endorsed by the World Design Organization)
entryFee: Free during the initial registration period (through Jul 1, 2026); RMB 3,500 (~US$510) per entry for late registration through the Sep 1, 2026 deadline
prizeMoney: Total prize pool of approximately €500,000: ¥1,000,000 Grand Award (1 winner); Product Group: Gold ¥300,000 each (4 winners), Silver ¥100,000 each (16 winners), Bronze ¥30,000 each (20 winners); Concept Group: Future Talents ¥20,000 each (4 winners), Young Talents trophies/certificates (10 winners)
shortDescription: A China-based, WDO-endorsed industrial design award with a roughly €500,000 total prize pool, spanning Product Group and Concept Group tracks across four sectors.
submissionFormat: Online registration with project documentation; video documentation is mandatory for non-physical products and required for all entries advancing to the second evaluation round
longDescription: The Design Intelligence Award (DIA) is endorsed by the World Design Organization and organized in China, evaluating entries across two groups, Product (market-ready designs) and Concept (forward-looking proposals, including a dedicated Young Talents track), spanning four sectors: Digital Economy, Industrial Equipment, Life Wisdom, and Cultural Innovation. The competition is open to enterprises, universities, institutions, and individuals worldwide, with free registration during an initial window followed by a paid late-registration period. The 2026 cycle offers a total prize pool of roughly €500,000, including a ¥1,000,000 Grand Award.

title: Archiproducts Design Awards 2026
entryFee: €900 per product (single submission); €600 for each additional product from the same brand; +€200 supplementary fee for entries in the Sustainability category
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive physical awards, certificates, and digital/branding recognition, celebrated at an in-person ceremony (past editions held at Superstudio Più, Milan)
shortDescription: An Italian product design competition from Archiproducts recognizing furniture, lighting, bathroom, kitchen, and building-material design, with a dedicated Sustainability category.
submissionFormat: Online nomination via the Archiproducts Design Awards portal: product images and supporting details, submitted by the manufacturer or brand (1 to 5 products per brand, launched or presented between June 2025 and September 2026)
longDescription: Now in its 11th edition, the Archiproducts Design Awards is an international product design competition run by Archiproducts, the Italian architecture and design products platform headquartered in Bari, Italy. Brands and manufacturers nominate products across categories including furniture, bathroom, kitchen, outdoor, office, contract, lighting, wellness, décor, finishes, building shell, construction, and systems/materials, plus a dedicated Sustainability category judged separately with an additional fee. The jury has included figures such as the Head of Design at David Chipperfield Architects and leadership from Zaha Hadid Architects. Winners are celebrated at an in-person ceremony, with past editions held at Superstudio Più in Milan.

title: AN's 2026 Best of Design Awards
entryFee: $295 general entry (Aug 1 – Sep 18, 2026, 11:59pm ET); $150 for emerging firms (founded within the last five years), applicable across all categories
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners are published in AN's print Best of Design 2026 issue and featured across AN's editorial platforms to over 1 million AEC-industry readers
shortDescription: An annual awards program from The Architect's Newspaper honoring standout architecture and interiors projects across more than 50 categories reflecting AN's editorial coverage.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the AN Best of Design registration portal: project images, a written description, and supporting materials per category
longDescription: The Architect's Newspaper's Best of Design Awards recognize outstanding work across more than 50 categories spanning infrastructure, landscape, facades, civic and cultural buildings, homes, ADUs, and interiors. Entries are judged on strength of presentation, evidence of innovation, creative use of technology, sustainability, and overall design quality. Projects must have been completed within two years of the submission deadline (landscape, public, and unbuilt projects within three years). Winners are published in AN's print Best of Design issue and promoted across the publication's editorial platforms.

title: Architectural Products Product Innovation Awards 2026
entryFee: $275 per entry, with a $150 discount on the second and subsequent entries in the same program; reduced pricing applies during early-entry windows
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive a PIA 2026 logo for use in marketing materials, plus feature coverage on the Architectural Products website and in the November/December 2026 print issue
shortDescription: A US trade-publication award from Architectural Products magazine recognizing innovative building products across categories from lighting and facades to finishes and hardware.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the Architectural Products Product Innovation Awards portal: product details and supporting images per category
longDescription: The Product Innovation Awards, run by Architectural Products magazine (part of Endeavor Business Media's Buildings & Construction group), honor products, systems, and materials that elevate architectural creativity and performance. Categories span acoustics, appliances and plumbing, building materials and facades, finishes and surfaces, furnishings, hardware, lighting, openings, roofing, textiles, and technology. Products launched between December 2023 and December 2026 are eligible. Winners are featured on the Architectural Products website and in the magazine's November/December print issue, and may use the PIA 2026 logo in their own marketing.

title: Graphis Design Awards 2027
entryFee: Member Single entry $70 / Non-Member Single entry $140; Member Series/Video entry $140 / Non-Member Series/Video entry $280 (Graphis Members save 50%)
prizeMoney: No cash prize: Platinum, Gold, and Silver winners are published on graphis.com and receive recognition among global creative directors and design leaders
shortDescription: An annual professional graphic design competition from Graphis spanning brand identity, packaging, editorial, typography, environmental, and digital design.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the Graphis entry platform: a single image for standalone work, or a series (up to six additional images) for campaigns, branding systems, or multi-spread publications
longDescription: Graphis Design Awards is an annual professional-only graphic design competition run by Graphis, Inc., the New York publisher behind the Poster, Advertising, Photography, and New Talent competitions. Categories include Brand Identity, Packaging, Editorial, Typography, Environmental, Digital Design, Gaming, and Poster Design. A single entry is one image (a poster, cover, ad, logo, photograph, or illustration); a series entry covers campaigns, branding systems, or multi-spread publications. Platinum and Gold-winning work is published on graphis.com and viewed by creative directors and design leaders worldwide; student work is directed instead to Graphis's separate New Talent competition.

title: International Architecture Awards 2027
organizer: The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design / The European Centre for Architecture Art Design and Urban Studies
entryFee: €395 per project
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winning architects prepare framed drawings or photographic panels and models for exhibition; projects are published on the Museum's website or in a catalogue, with past exhibitions held in cities including London, Brussels, and Istanbul
shortDescription: A prestigious international architecture award from The Chicago Athenaeum and The European Centre recognizing outstanding new buildings, landscape architecture, and urban planning projects worldwide.
submissionFormat: Online application via chi-athenaeum.org: 10-12 project images (16:9 or 1:1 aspect ratio, 300dpi, max 6MB each), a 500-700 word project description in English, and a single PDF (plans, sections, elevations); file names must use Latin characters only
longDescription: The International Architecture Awards are presented jointly by The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design and The European Centre for Architecture Art Design and Urban Studies, recognizing the world's most outstanding new buildings, interiors, landscapes, and urban planning projects. The award is open to international architects and firms (including U.S.-based firms submitting international or domestic work), with eligible projects designed or built after January 1, 2024. Categories span more than 15 building types, including airports, bridges, commercial and corporate buildings, hospitals, hotels, offices, residential, retail, schools, religious structures, urban planning, landscape architecture, and restorations; previously awarded projects are ineligible. Winning projects are exhibited internationally and published by the Museum.

title: The Quiet Tower International Architecture Competition
entryFee: Advanced tier (23 Jul – 15 Oct 2026): €120 professional / €110 student; Last Minute tier (16 Oct 2026 – 13 Jan 2027): €140 professional / €120 student, plus 4.5% VAT; installment payment available
prizeMoney: €10,000 total prize fund: 1st €5,000, 2nd €2,500, 3rd €1,000, plus a €1,000 Buildner Student Award, a €500 Buildner Sustainability Award, and 6 honourable mentions with certificates
shortDescription: An open international architecture ideas competition from Buildner inviting designs for an observation tower on Latvia's remote Cape Kolka coastline.
submissionFormat: Online registration and submission via architecturecompetitions.com: full design brief with CAD site files and reference photos/videos provided; entries and correspondence must be in English
longDescription: The Quiet Tower is an international architecture ideas competition organized by Buildner, inviting architects, designers, students, and enthusiasts worldwide to reimagine an observation tower on the Baltic coastline at Cape Kolka, Latvia. Rather than an iconic landmark, the brief calls for a 'lookout ritual,' a structure emphasizing atmosphere and emotional connection inspired by fire lookout towers and Nordic retreat culture. The competition is open to all with no professional qualification required, and entries can be submitted individually or by teams of up to four. The €10,000 prize fund includes dedicated Student and Sustainability awards alongside the main placements.

title: Andrew Martin International Interior Designer of the Year Award 2027
entryFee: Not publicly disclosed on andrewmartin.co.uk; entrants apply via a downloadable PDF application form rather than a listed fee schedule
prizeMoney: No cash prize: the winner and a shortlisted international 'Top 100' are published in the Andrew Martin Interior Design Review, a 500-page annual hardcover volume, and profiled on andrewmartin.co.uk; the overall Designer of the Year is chosen by a panel of celebrity judges (2025 judges included Stanley Tucci and Felicity Blunt)
shortDescription: A prestigious global interior design award from British furniture brand Andrew Martin, dubbed 'the Oscars of the design world,' recognizing a Designer of the Year from an international 'Top 100' shortlist.
submissionFormat: Downloadable PDF application form submitted directly to Andrew Martin, per the process outlined at andrewmartin.co.uk/design-awards
longDescription: Running since 1996 and described by The Sunday Times as 'the Oscars of the Design World,' the Andrew Martin International Interior Designer of the Year Award is presented by the British luxury furniture and interiors brand Andrew Martin. Professional interior designers from around the world submit residential and commercial projects for consideration; a shortlist of roughly 100 designers is published each year in the Andrew Martin Interior Design Review, often called 'the bible of interior design.' A panel of celebrity judges then selects the overall Designer of the Year from the international entrants.

title: WorldStar 2027 Global Packaging Awards
entryFee: €650 for the first entry, €500 for each additional entry; Special Award category entries (Sustainability, Marketing, Packaging that Saves Food, Accessible Packaging) are €650 each and require an entry in a main category first
prizeMoney: No cash prize: winners receive a WorldStar trophy and certificate, worldwide media recognition, and rights to use the winner's logo on packaging and promotional materials
shortDescription: The world's most prestigious packaging design award, presented by the World Packaging Organisation, open only to packs that have already won a WPO-recognized national or regional packaging competition.
submissionFormat: Online submission via worldstar.org: category selection, a 500-word written justification of the pack, and up to 5 high-resolution images (combined file size under 5MB); payment due by November 2, 2026
longDescription: WorldStar is the global packaging awards program of the World Packaging Organisation (WPO), widely regarded as the pre-eminent international recognition for packaging design, innovation, and sustainability. Entry is restricted to packaging that has already won an award in one of roughly 75-85 WPO-recognized national or regional packaging competitions in the current or previous year. There is no direct-entry route for unproven packs. Categories span major packaging types alongside Special Awards for Sustainability, Marketing, Packaging that Saves Food, and Accessible Packaging. Around 200 winners are typically selected from 300+ qualifying entries spanning 30+ countries, with winners honored at an international gala tied to a major packaging trade fair.

title: ADI Compasso d'Oro International Award 2027 (IV Edition)
organizer: ADI - Associazione per il Disegno Industriale (Italian Association for Industrial Design)
country: International (open to designers/companies from Expo 2027 Belgrade participating countries)
entryFee: €1,000 per product entry
prizeMoney: 20 Compasso d'Oro Awards plus up to 50 Honourable Mentions; recognition-based, no fixed cash prize specified in the regulations
shortDescription: The fourth edition of the international spin-off of Italy's historic Compasso d'Oro, ADI's design prize running since 1954, themed 'Play for Humanity: Sport and Music for All' in partnership with Expo 2027 Belgrade.
submissionFormat: Online submission via compassodorointernational.com including product photographs, a written description, and a short video (max. 60 seconds, smartphone footage acceptable) in English
longDescription: The ADI Compasso d'Oro International Award extends the legacy of Italy's oldest and most prestigious industrial design prize (established 1954) to an international stage. This fourth edition is organized in collaboration with Expo 2027 Belgrade and centers on the theme 'Play for Humanity: Sport and Music for All'. Entries span nine categories including Design for Living, Lighting, Mobility, Work, the Individual, Food Design, Service and Social Design, Communication Design, and Exhibition Design. Products must already be released to market in one of the countries participating in Expo 2027 Belgrade. Submissions are reviewed by ADI's expert jury, with winners announced at a ceremony in Belgrade.

title: MIAW Innovation 2026 (Muuuz International Awards)
entryFee: Paid per-product entry fee; exact 2026 amount not published in sources found this session
prizeMoney: Winners receive a MIAW trophy at a Paris award ceremony; no cash prize amount found in sources checked this session
shortDescription: Annual French interior-products award from Muuuz/ArchiDesignClub recognizing the most outstanding products in architecture, interior design, and decoration, with an Innovation-focused track alongside its Design track.
submissionFormat: Online registration via miaw.muuuz.com with product images and a technical/design description
longDescription: The Muuuz International Awards (MIAW), run by French design and architecture media outlet Muuuz (ArchiDesignClub, Groupe Ficade), have recognized outstanding products in architecture, interior design, and decoration for over a decade. The Innovation edition highlights a product's technical, functional, and virtuous qualities across four categories: Interior Equipment/Furnishing, Materials and Coatings, Lighting, and Outdoor. Winners are presented with trophies at award ceremonies held at venues in Paris, including the Grand Hôtel InterContinental Paris.

title: The One Show 2027 — Design & Branding
entryFee: Tiered entry fee that increases at each of four deadline periods (Early, Regular, Extended, Final); exact 2027 amounts not yet published
prizeMoney: Winners receive Pencil trophies (Gold/Silver/Bronze/Merit) in the Design & Branding discipline; no cash prize
shortDescription: The Design & Branding discipline of The One Show, one of the advertising and design industry's longest-running global creative awards, run by The One Club for Creativity in New York.
submissionFormat: Online entry via oneshow.org; several Design & Branding categories additionally require physical entry materials mailed to The One Club
longDescription: The One Show is one of the creative industry's most prestigious international awards programs, run annually by The One Club for Creativity. Alongside its advertising disciplines, it includes dedicated 'Design & Branding' and 'Design in Advertising' categories recognizing excellence in brand identity, packaging, environmental and editorial design, and related visual communication work. Entries for the 2027 cycle open October 27, 2026, with a series of escalating-fee deadlines running through early March 2027. Winners are celebrated with the program's iconic Pencil trophies during Creative Week in New York City.

title: DETAIL Architecture Award 2027
entryFee: Processing fee applies to all entries, with a reduced Early Bird rate for submissions by 30 September 2026 and a discount for DETAIL magazine/DETAIL Inspiration subscribers; exact amounts not published in sources found this session
prizeMoney: Award recognition and feature publication in DETAIL magazine; no cash prize amount found in sources checked this session

longDescription: Presented by the German Design Council (the same body behind the German Design Award), the German Brand Award recognizes companies, agencies, and institutions whose branding and marketing work sets new standards. Entrants register and nominate projects across categories spanning corporate and product brand work, judged by an independent expert jury. The award draws over 1,300 submissions annually from around 20 countries, with winners celebrated at an Awards Show in Berlin.

longDescription: Now marking its 25th edition, the Andreu World International Design Contest invites students and professionals worldwide to design seating and tables referencing Andreu World's product lines. A jury of leading design professionals, including figures from Foster & Partners and the World Design Organization, judges submissions, which require a 1:5 scale physical model plus a technical report.

longDescription: Organized by the Simon brand in collaboration with the Fundació Mies van der Rohe, the Living Places – Simon Architecture Prize recognizes built projects, including interiors, public spaces, and landscaping, completed between January 2024 and December 2025. Two winning projects each receive €10,000 and an exclusive piece designed by Andreu Carulla; finalists are announced in December, with the award ceremony in February.
